title: fix: require confirmed fraud before an automatic ban
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
Radar escalates its risk level on every retry of an already-declined card, so a paying customer with a retry storm can out-score a card tester on volume alone. One live account shows this: 1,400 charges from **2 cards**, $1,523 spent, no dispute and no fraud report, but 963 blocked and 399 highest-risk charges all inside a single month of retries after `insufficient_funds`.

- A ban now also requires one signal confirmed after the fact: a fraudulent dispute, a fraud report, or an early fraud warning.
- Radar's blocked and highest-risk flags still raise the score, but never convict on their own.
- `collectStripeFraudScores` returns the set of users with confirmed evidence; `runFraudBanCheck` requires it alongside the threshold.
- Of the 23 candidates in the simulator, 22 already carry confirmed evidence, so this removes one account and protects legitimate customers at any threshold.
- Test: 600 blocked highest-risk charges on one customer ban nobody; adding a single fraud warning to the same history bans.

The simulator mirrors this rule so the two cannot drift.

gist.headline: The hive checks the evidence
gist.blurb: A noisy card retry storm no longer gets to impersonate a fraud verdict. Polli now waits for confirmed evidence before closing the garden gate.
gist.summary: Automatic Stripe fraud bans now require both the existing risk-score threshold and confirmed post-event evidence—a fraudulent dispute, fraud report, or early fraud warning—while the simulator mirrors the same rule.
gist.impact: Legitimate customers with repeated insufficient-funds retries can remain active even when Radar marks many attempts blocked or highest-risk, while accounts with confirmed fraud evidence still qualify for automatic bans.
gist.visual_concept: Depict fraud scoring as a cozy garden gate: a pile of noisy retry papers and red risk flags raises a gauge, but Polli only closes the gate after examining a clearly stamped confirmed-evidence document. Include gentle code-plants and a small monitor robot holding the score readout, emphasizing careful verification rather than punishment.
